items.title: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals - Reuters
items.summary: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals    Reuters
items.raw_description: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals    Reuters

items.title: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals
items.author: David Lawder, Antoni Slodkowski
items.creator: David Lawder, Antoni Slodkowski
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet on Sunday to try to tee up potential agreements on AI, tariffs and critical minerals for a high-stakes Washington summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
items.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet on Sunday to try to tee up potential agreements on AI, tariffs and critical minerals for a high-stakes Washington summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The meetings at JP Morgan Chase's (JPM.N) headquarters in Manhattan, which also will include US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, are due to start at about 10:30 a.m. (1430 GMT) and are expected to run all day.
Key topics will be the status of a US-China trade truce that is set to expire on November 10, flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets and critical minerals that US officials say are insufficient and potential guard rails for artificial intelligence after reports of key security breaches involving AI models.
The most likely outcome, analysts say, would be for Washington and Beijing to agree on small steps to show they are continuing to avoid escalating tensions in a delicate trade relationship that has major consequences for the global economy.
"I think there will be some show of deliverables because of the fact that it's a presidential summit coming, but I don't feel like we're on the verge of some sort of breakthrough," said Anna Ashton, a longtime China trade analyst and founder of Ashton Intelligence. "I think status quo is probably both sides' general best expectation."
Many of the issues that He, Bessent and Greer will have to work through for Trump and Xi are holdovers from the two leaders' [USN:L6N41R1CR TEXT:"meeting in Beijing"] in May, including an effort on both sides to cut tariffs on non-strategic goods and Chinese pledges to increase purchases of US agricultural goods by $17 billion a year and to purchase more than 200 Boeing aircraft.
The Bessent-He-Greer meeting follows a pattern set over the past 16 months, in which the three officials met in European and Asian cities to tee up potential agreements for Trump and Xi. These efforts included the November 2025 truce reached in Busan, South Korea, which capped US tariffs imposed during Trump's second term in office at about 20% on Chinese goods after tit-for-tat escalation had brought them to triple-digit levels on both sides.
The US Supreme Court later [USN:L6N3ZH003 TEXT:"struck down"] the Trump tariffs that were invoked under a national emergencies law, including duties related to fentanyl trafficking.
Trump's administration has been rebuilding them under new authorities, including restoring a 12.5% tariff on Chinese goods over forced labor allegations. It is finalizing a separate tariff investigation aimed at curbing excess industrial capacity that it says is rampant in China.
Under that truce, China promised to restore the flow of critical minerals to US and global users. However, a senior US official told reporters on Friday that China's performance on that front "has not been up to par" and would be a topic for discussion ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
NEW TALKS ON AI The Bessent-He discussions on AI are significant because the US and China are the [USN:L1N45700J TEXT:"two major forces"] driving development of advanced AI tools and the global adoption of the technology. Rare earths play a crucial role in the manufacturing of advanced semiconductor technology powering AI.
Bessent said on Friday he expects the discussions to cover [USN:L6N45A12D TEXT:""both open- and closed-weight models.""] Open-weight models are AI systems with publicly accessible core elements where users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks.
Chinese open-weight models are becoming more popular with US companies because they can be cheaper than closed-weight AI tools such as those developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and other US companies.
"The United States remains the leader in AI. And we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems," Bessent said in a statement regarding the China talks.
Bessent has called for the US and China to agree on AI "guard rails" aimed at keeping powerful models out of the hands of malign non-state actors.
TARIFF REDUCTIONS, INVESTMENT The US and China also agreed in May to launch discussions to reduce tariffs for non-strategic goods under a so-called "Board of Trade" mechanism along with a similar forum to deal with specific investment issues.
While the Trump administration has tightened restrictions on US companies investing in some industries in China, Reuters reported on Friday that it is [USN:L1N4570SO TEXT:"working on rules"] that would likely allow US pharmaceutical firms to invest in promising Chinese drugs and strike licensing deals for them.
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that He would also lead a delegation of Chinese companies to the US that would participate in economic and trade consultations ahead of the summit.
The business delegation, which mirrors a [USN:L1N41T02Q TEXT:"group of US CEOs"] that Trump brought to Beijing in May, was announced as Trump expressed openness to Chinese automakers building US factories. US auto industry groups on Friday [USN:L1N45A0MO TEXT:"urged Trump to maintain an effective ban"] on Chinese vehicle sales in the US on national security grounds.

items.title: World leaders return to UN amid wars in Middle East and Ukraine
items.author: Antoni Slodkowski
items.creator: Antoni Slodkowski
items.summary: World leaders gather in New York this week for the UN General Assembly, bracing for President Donald Trump's return to the rostrum for a second year running, with talks centering on the widening conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and the risks of artificial intelligence.
items.body:
World leaders [USN:L6N45312R TEXT:"gather"] in New York this week for the UN General Assembly , bracing for President Donald Trump's return to the rostrum for a second year running, with [USN:L6N45312R TEXT:"talks centering"] on the widening conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and the risks of artificial intelligence.
Nearly 130 heads of state meet with the post-World War Two order under strain and with the UN itself struggling to remain relevant and weathering attacks from Trump, who has slashed America's contributions and withdrawn from dozens of UN bodies.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who last addressed the diplomatic jamboree via video in 2021, will skip New York in favor of one-on-one talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, fueling debate about the UN's relevance in addressing global crises.
Compounding the crisis of morale and finance are questions about the next leader of the 80-year-old organization: Secretary-General Antonio Guterres completes his term at the end of 2026, with no clear frontrunner in the [USN:L6N3W20WS TEXT:"race"] to replace him.
The 15-member UN Security Council may hold high-level meetings on Ukraine, AI and the Middle East, including talks with Arab leaders, diplomats said.
More than a year into Trump's second term, "we would no longer say that the UN is in freefall, but we would say that it's stuck in an open-ended crisis," said Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group.
"The UN may not be in emergency care like it was last year, but it seems to be trapped in a trauma center for the foreseeable future," Gowan said.
The US avoided losing its vote at the assembly by paying $725 million in contributions to the regular budget this week, but it still owes the organization more than a billion dollars and makes ongoing demands for cuts and reforms.
GROWING AI RISKS The assembly meets shortly after several artificial intelligence industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown of the [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"development"] of the technology, [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"warning"] that it could soon improve on its own and escape human control.
Guterres has said that AI will be a major topic, adding that countries pushing its frontiers should set up "common guardrails in order to avoid this race to the bottom that could lead one day to a gigantic disaster at the global level."
The secretary-general has long proposed global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created an advisory body on the technology, with members including tech executives, government officials and academics.
The warning has put Guterres at odds with Trump, who dismissed AI risks as a "hoax," saying there is a "sick conspiracy" against it and that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on its development.
MIDDLE EAST ESCALATION The Middle East will again be a focus of discussions, as the [USN:FWN4580MR TEXT:"US-Israeli war on Iran"] continues to drive global inflation and destabilize the region. Recent gains by Houthi militants threaten shipping in the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and could further spike energy prices.
"It's very difficult to have a military solution for that problem, and the experience of fighting in Yemen demonstrated how complicated it is to have successful interventions," said Guterres, adding that the UN's envoy on Yemen was making a "huge effort" to advance talks.
Peace talks remain stalled, however, as Iran and the US continue to exchange strikes and Trump threatens a major escalation of the war.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza that Israel denies – is to speak on Thursday.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas will for the second year running not be at the gathering in person. The US, a close Israeli ally, again denied him a visa. On Thursday, the General Assembly voted to allow Abbas to appear via video.
There is likely to be a high-level meeting on the [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"conflict in Sudan"] on the sidelines, diplomats said, although a diplomatic breakthrough is unlikely.
UKRAINE, FOOD SECURITY Also on the agenda is Russia's more than four-year-old war in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will address the General Assembly. Zelenskiy will likely seek to shore up Ukraine's position ahead of what is expected to be another tough winter, diplomats said.
The Security Council has been unable to take action to end the conflict because permanent member Russia holds a veto.
Trump has at times appeared frustrated that he has been unable to broker an end to the war, a goal he declared a priority when he began his second term in January last year. The US president spoke with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin earlier this month, but it was unclear whether he plans to meet Zelenskiy in New York.
Guterres highlighted the impact the war was having on civilians but also on food security and energy prices.
"The effective blockade existing in the Black Sea is creating enormous problems that add to the problems generated by the Middle East crisis, and I think it would be very important to find a way to allow Ukrainian exports and Russian exports of food, fertilizers and energy to take place in a safe way through the Black Sea," he said.

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝Ｗソックス村上が先制適時打、カブス鈴木2安打1打点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１９日、各地で試合を行い、ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はタイガース戦に「４番・一塁」で出場。一回に先制適時打を放ち、４打数１安打１打点、２三振だった。ホワイトソックスは３─１で勝った。

カブスの鈴木誠也外野手はレッズ戦に「３番・指名打者」で出場。３打数２安打１打点、１四球、１三振だった。カブスは５─２で勝利した。

ブルージェイズの岡本和真内野手はレンジャーズ戦に「６番・三塁」で出場し、４打数１安打。ブルージェイズは２─６で負けた。

パドレスの松井裕樹投手はマーリンズ戦、１点リードの七回に４番手として登板。２／３回で１安打無失点、１四球だった。パドレスは延長十回の末、７─６でサヨナラ勝ち。連勝を４に伸ばした。

items.title: サッカー＝バルセロナ開幕7連勝、ラフィーニャがハットトリック
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［セビリア（スペイン）　１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［セビリア（スペイン）　１９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は１９日、各地で試合を行い、バルセロナはセビリアを３─１で下し、開幕７連勝を飾った。

バルセロナは前半１９分に失点するも、すぐに反撃。その３分後にラフィーニャが同点弾を挙げると、後半７分には頭で加点し、同２４分には相手守備陣の裏に抜け出し、ハットトリックを達成した。

今季７試合で１２得点としたラフィーニャは、得点ランキングトップにつけている。

その他、セルタはラシンに５─０と圧勝し、今季初勝利。ビルバオとアラベスはスコアレスドローで試合を終え、オサスナはラヨ・バリェカノと１─１で引き分けた。

items.title: Rookie Ethan Salas lifts Padres past Marlins in 10 innings
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning Saturday night and the San Diego Padres edged the visiting Miami Marlins 7-6.
items.body:
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning Saturday night and the San Diego Padres edged the visiting Miami Marlins 7-6.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). After Sung-Mun Song fanned, Salas batted for Freddy Fermin and grounded a 0-2 fastball up the middle for San Diego's 11th walk-off win of the year.
David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69, a game ahead of Philadelphia, and reduced their magic number for clinching a playoff spot to three.
Miami (76-79) forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth. It was Conine's 17th homer of the year.
Both starters did not factor into the decision after rough outings. Miami right-hander Eury Perez permitted five runs on eight hits and three walks in 4 2/3 innings, whiffing four. San Diego righty Casey Mize lasted only three innings, allowing five hits and five runs while walking five and striking out two.
The Marlins initiated scoring with three runs in the second, Joe Mack's fielder's choice scored Jakob Marsee, and Otto Lopez cracked a two-run homer over the left field wall, his 11th of the year.
Samad Taylor got the Padres on the board in their half of the second with his second homer of the season, a 388-foot shot to left. But Miami upped the lead to 5-1 in the third as Agustin Ramirez grounded an RBI-double down the left field line and scored on Esteury Ruiz's single.
San Diego rallied for three runs in the third. Cronenworth coaxed a bases-loaded walk and Ty France scored on a balk by Perez, followed by a sacrifice fly by Taylor.
Fernando Tatis Jr. drew the Padres even at 5-5 in the fourth when he rifled a leadoff homer an estimated 410 feet to right-center, his 24th of the year. They took the lead in the sixth when France ripped a two-out double just over the head of Ruiz in right, scoring Dustin Harris.
--Field Level Media

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝オリオールズ、守護神バティスタ投手が約1年ぶりに復帰
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）オリオールズは１９日、右肩のけがで６０日間の負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）に入っていた守護神フェリックス・バティスタ投手（３１）をロースターに登録した。

バティスタが最後にメジャーの試合に出場したのは昨年７月２０日のレイズ戦。この試合でシーズン１９セーブ目を挙げていた。同年８月１９日、右肩の手術を受けていた。

バティスタは２０２３年、オールスターに選出されたが、同年８月２５日のロッキーズ戦で右肘の内側側副靱帯を痛め、シーズン残り試合を欠場。トミー・ジョン手術（靱帯再建手術）を受けたため、２４年シーズンは全休だった。

同投手はメジャーでの３年間で通算１５６試合に登板。１３勝７敗６７セーブ、防御率２．０１を記録している。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝結腸がん克服したマンシーニ、古巣オリオールズで引退
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のトレイ・マンシーニ一塁手（３４）が１９日、古巣オリオールズと１日の契約を結んだ後、正式に現役を引退した。

マンシーニはメジャーで８年プレー。２０１６年から２２年途中までオリオールズで過ごした。オリオールズはこの日、ホームでのブルワーズ戦の前に、マンシーニのキャリアをたたえるセレモニーを行った。

マンシーニは１３年ドラフト８巡目でオリオールズから指名された。２０年にステージ３の結腸がんと診断され、同年のシーズンを全休。復帰した２１年に打率２割５分５厘、２１本塁打、７１打点をマークしてカムバック賞を受賞した。

２４年と２５年はメジャーでプレーせず、今年はエンゼルスで５試合に出場。６月１７日に事実上の戦力外となっていた。メジャーでの通算成績は打率２割６分３厘、１２９本塁打、４０４打点。２２年にアストロズでワールドシリーズ優勝を達成した。

items.title: Dernier jour des élections législatives en Russie
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les élections législatives en Russie, présentées par le président Vladimir Poutine comme un baromètre du soutien à la guerre contre l'Ukraine, sont entrées dimanche dans leur troisième et dernier jour.
items.body:
Les élections législatives en Russie, présentées par le président Vladimir Poutine comme un baromètre du soutien à la guerre contre l'Ukraine, sont entrées dimanche dans leur troisième et dernier jour.
Le parti au pouvoir, "Russie unie", devrait conserver sa position dominante au sein d'un système politique qui, selon ses détracteurs, ne tolère pas la dissidence.
Le scrutin, qui vise à renouveler les 450 sièges de la chambre basse du Parlement, la Douma d'Etat, est le premier organisé depuis que la Russie a lancé son invasion à grande échelle en Ukraine en février 2022.
La plupart des candidats opposés à la guerre ont été exclus du scrutin après que la Cour suprême a jugé que le parti libéral Iabloko, qui réclame un cessez-le-feu en Ukraine, avait enfreint les règles électorales. Certains de ses candidats se sont toutefois présentés dans certaines circonscriptions.
Le Kremlin affirme que l'unité nationale et une certaine censure sont nécessaires pendant la guerre en Ukraine, qu'il qualifie d'opération militaire spéciale.
Vladimir Poutine a accusé vendredi l'Ukraine d'[USN:L6N45A196 TEXT:"ingérence"] dans les élections, citant en exemple une frappe ukrainienne ayant récemment touché un village situé dans une zone de Zaporijjia occupée par la Russie, tuant une responsable au sein de la commission électorale locale.
Les autorités russes ont par ailleurs signalé samedi une [USN:L8N45B03A TEXT:"cyberattaque"] contre les systèmes de vote en ligne à Moscou.
Les premiers résultats devraient commencer à être communiqués vers 18h00 GMT dimanche, les résultats complets étant attendus lundi.

items.title: Van dominates Pantoja to retain flyweight belt in UFC 331
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury.
items.body:
Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury.
Pantoja had suffered an [USN:L6N3XD00V TEXT:"accidental elbow dislocation"] 26 seconds into their first fight in December last year, resulting in Van becoming the UFC flyweight champion without an outright win over the Brazilian, who had reigned over the division for over two years.
Van, the first UFC champion from Myanmar, defended the belt against Tatsuro Taira in May but was left waiting until Saturday to seal his status as the best in the division as 36-year-old Pantoja recovered from the injury.
"A lot of people said that was an accidental win... well, doubt me now," said Joshua after his second title defence that extended his professional MMA record to 18 wins and two losses.
Pantoja took Van down in the first round, before landing heavy punches and knees in a fiery exchange, as Van retaliated with a slicing elbow.
"You're too good to brawl with this guy," Van's coaches told him during the break, suggesting a more tactical approach.
Van peppered Pantoja with left-handed jabs in the second round, and rocked the Brazilian with a fluid combination of punches in the third. Pantoja controlled the fourth round as he took Van down but was unable to submit him.
In the final round, Van stalked Pantoja and knocked him down with an overhand right, securing the win in the judges' scorecards.
In the co-main event, Armenian contender Arman Tsarukyan staked his claim for a shot at the lightweight title when he pinned Maurício Ruffy to the cage, rocked him with a left elbow and knocked him out with a right elbow with four seconds to spare in the first round.
"I knew my time would come, so I was patient," said Tsarukyan, who extended his win streak to six fights, as he called for a bout with champion Justin Gaethje.

Sept 19 : Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury.
Pantoja had suffered an accidental elbow dislocation 26 seconds into their first fight in December last year, resulting in Van becoming the UFC flyweight champion without an outright win over the Brazilian, who had reigned over the division for over two years.
Van, the first UFC champion from Myanmar, defended the belt against Tatsuro Taira in May but was left waiting until Saturday to seal his status as the best in the division as 36-year-old Pantoja recovered from the injury.
"A lot of people said that was an accidental win... well, doubt me now," said Joshua after his second title defence that extended his professional MMA record to 18 wins and two losses.

Pantoja took Van down in the first round, before landing heavy punches and knees in a fiery exchange, as Van retaliated with a slicing elbow.
"You're too good to brawl with this guy," Van's coaches told him during the break, suggesting a more tactical approach.
Van peppered Pantoja with left-handed jabs in the second round, and rocked the Brazilian with a fluid combination of punches in the third. Pantoja controlled the fourth round as he took Van down but was unable to submit him.
In the final round, Van stalked Pantoja and knocked him down with an overhand right, securing the win in the judges' scorecards.
In the co-main event, Armenian contender Arman Tsarukyan staked his claim for a shot at the lightweight title when he pinned Maurício Ruffy to the cage, rocked him with a left elbow and knocked him out with a right elbow with four seconds to spare in the first round.
"I knew my time would come, so I was patient," said Tsarukyan, who extended his win streak to six fights, as he called for a bout with champion Justin Gaethje.

items.title: Malaysian ex-PM Najib working on conditions to start house arrest, his lawyers say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Malaysia's jailed former prime minister, Najib Razak, is working to fulfil the conditions to leave jail and begin his house arrest, including paying a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine, his lawyers said on Sunday.
items.body:
Malaysia's jailed former prime minister, Najib Razak, is working to fulfil the conditions to leave jail and begin his [USN:L6N45A03A TEXT:"house arrest"], including paying a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine, his lawyers said on Sunday.
Najib's ability to satisfy the condition "do not lie in his own hands" as a significant part of his assets, bank accounts and properties remain subject to freeze orders and enforcement proceedings by the government, the lawyers said in a statement.
Najib, prime minister from 2009 to 2018, was found guilty of corruption in relation to the [USN:L6N3XT06B TEXT:"embezzlement"] of billions of dollars tied to 1Malaysia Development Berhad, a state investment fund he co-founded while in power. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.
Malaysia's king agreed on Friday to let Najib Razak leave jail and serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. It was the second royal pardon over his conviction for his involvement in a multi-billion-dollar financial scandal.
Malaysia's Prisons Department said in a statement on Sunday that it and the home affairs ministry were waiting for official written confirmation of the pardon before taking any action. By law, the home affairs minister has the power to gazette any premises as a prison, which could be used to designate Najib’s home as a place to serve his sentence.
Najib has been "deeply moved" by the support he has received from the public, the lawyers said.
The president of Najib's UMNO party, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said on Friday that a collection fund would be launched for party members and supporters to help Najib pay for the fine. The party had raised almost 1 million ringgit by Saturday noon, local media reported.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's multi-party government, which includes the DAP as well as Najib’s UMNO, has seen growing rifts over the government's response to issues of corruption.

items.title: Macron va rencontrer Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Emmanuel Macron rencontrera dimanche le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, quelques semaines après que le président américain Donald Trump a publié sur les réseaux sociaux une image montrant l’archipel recouvert du drapeau américain.
items.body:
Emmanuel Macron rencontrera dimanche le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, quelques semaines après que le président américain Donald Trump a publié sur les réseaux sociaux une image montrant l’archipel recouvert du drapeau américain.
Cette visite, la première d'un président français depuis celle effectuée par François Hollande en 2014, intervient alors que le Canada cherche à renforcer ses liens avec l'Union européenne dans un contexte de tensions commerciales avec les Etats-Unis et de détérioration des relations avec Washington.
A son arrivée dans l'archipel samedi soir, Emmanuel Macron a rappelé que Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon restait un territoire français.
"C'est une évidence pour nous que c'est un territoire français, et un territoire attaché à la France et fier d'être français", a dit aux journalistes le chef de l'Etat. "Nous y sommes attachés. Il n'y a pas de débat, il n'y a pas de discussion."
Un responsable de la présidence française avait déclaré plus tôt à la presse: "Pour un territoire de 5.800 habitants, il est rare de trouver autant d'enjeux importants pour la France concentrés dans un espace de cette taille: la présence géostratégique de la France dans l'Atlantique Nord, aux portes des Etats-Unis et de l'Arctique, la souveraineté maritime, l'adaptation au changement climatique, ainsi que la coopération avec le Canada."
Selon des diplomates, cette visite, qu'Emmanuel Macron effectue avant de se rendre à l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, revêt une importance symbolique, après que Donald Trump a publié une carte représentant les Etats-Unis, le Canada, le Groenland, l'Islande, le Mexique, l'Amérique centrale et les Caraïbes enveloppés dans le drapeau américain et portant la mention "Etats-Unis d'Amérique".
L'image incluait Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon ainsi que plusieurs territoires français des Caraïbes. La France avait alors choisi de ne pas réagir publiquement à cette publication.
Emmanuel Macron et Mark Carney devraient aborder la crise énergétique ainsi que les relations de plus en plus étroites entre le Canada et l'UE, après que celle-ci a ouvert la voie à une adhésion d'Ottawa en tant que premier membre associé.

items.title: Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
items.body:
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith hit a home run as the Dodgers (95-60) won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3.
Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings with three strikeouts. The left-hander is now 4-2 with a 2.85 ERA in nine starts for Los Angeles after a trade from the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 2.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants (64-91) while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
San Francisco lost for the sixth time in its past eight games in its next-to-last road game of the season.
Max Muncy had an RBI double in the first inning to score Betts as the Dodgers started a stretch in which they scored in each of the first six innings. Betts had an RBI single in the second.
The Giants tied the score in the third on Bericoto's fifth home run over his first 35 career games.
Los Angeles went back on top 3-2 in the third on Smith's leadoff home run. Both teams scored in the fourth, with San Francisco tying the score 4-4 in the fifth on a double from Jung Hoo Lee.
Edman's two-run single in the fifth gave the Dodgers the lead for good and they added another in the inning for a 7-4 lead on a Miguel Rojas single.
In the sixth, Smith added an RBI single, while rookie Josue De Paula followed with a two-run single for a 10-4 advantage.
Los Angeles has a 5-4 advantage in the season series with four games still remaining between the teams.
Smith went 3-for-5 as the Dodgers collected 15 hits.
Lee went 2-for-4 for the Giants and drove in a run. The Giants had two hits in a dozen at-bats with runners in scoring position.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Merz under pressure as two more German states go to the polls
items.author: James Mackenzie
items.creator: James Mackenzie
items.summary: German voters go to the polls on Sunday in two state elections that look likely to heap more pressure on struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose future has been in the balance since the far right's triumph in another regional vote this month.
items.body:
German voters go to the polls on Sunday in two state elections that look likely to heap more pressure on struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose future has been [USN:L8N4571NP TEXT:"in the balance"] since the far right's triumph in another regional vote this month.
The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in the formerly communist east, and the capital Berlin follow the [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"September 6 election"] in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority.
Regional elections would not usually draw much interest outside Germany, but the AfD's success in Saxony-Anhalt, which it sees as the first step towards winning federal elections due in 2029, has sent shock waves through Europe.
In just over a decade, the party, which wants to take tough action to deport foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, has transformed itself from a fringe eurosceptic movement to the country's most popular party.
Opinion polls indicate it is unlikely to repeat its victory in Saxony-Anhalt in either of Sunday's votes. But they are both expected to underscore the huge advances it has made in recent years and raise fresh questions over the so-called "firewall" strategy, under which the other main parties refuse to enter coalition agreements with it.
For Merz, whose approval ratings have plunged as low as 14%, according to the latest polls, the result was the latest in a series of blows that have raised growing doubts in his own conservative Christian Democratic Union party about whether he can continue to lead.
In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks likely to suffer its worst-ever election result, with the most recent opinion poll by the Forschungsgruppe Wahlen on Friday putting it at just 6% and at risk of failing to clear the minimum threshold to enter the state parliament.
MERZ HAS STRUGGLED Elected last year on a promise of ambitious reforms to return Germany's stagnant economy to growth, Merz has struggled to win over sceptical voters, compounding resentment over unpopular pension, tax and healthcare reforms with a stream of gaffes and communication missteps.
For the moment at least, [USN:L8N4580EF TEXT:"senior figures in the CDU"] have rallied behind him, aware that replacing the chancellor - which would in any case be difficult on constitutional grounds - would leave any successor facing the same deep economic problems.
But disillusion with his government has hung over the campaigns in both Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, where voters have focused on issues including soaring energy and housing costs.
Surging fuel prices, felt acutely in a state like Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania where many rely on cars for transport, have put pressure on Merz to agree relief measures with his Social Democrat coalition partners.
On Friday, [USN:L8N45A15I TEXT:"he presented"] a relief package that included tax cuts on gas and diesel.
In the rural state, polls have shown the race narrowing over recent weeks as the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) have centred their campaign around popular [USN:L8N4571NP TEXT:"state premier Manuela Schwesig"]. The Wahlen poll on Friday showed the SPD edging in front of the AfD for the first time in months.
The poll put the SPD on 37%, the AfD on 36%, the far-left Left Party on 9% and the environmental Greens on 5%, just at the threshold for entering parliament. Both parties would be potential coalition partners for Schwesig.
In Berlin, the Wahlen poll showed the far-left Left Party moving ahead of the CDU, threatening the conservative hold on the mayor's office in a campaign that has focused heavily on housing affordability. Even in liberal Berlin, however, the AfD has made strong gains, moving into third place.
The latest poll puts the Left Party on 22%, the CDU on 20%, the Greens on 15% and the SPD on 12%. The AfD sits on 18%, while the far-left BSW, the only party that has said it might agree to work with the AfD, is just under the parliamentary threshold on 4%.

items.title: Pavin Smith’s pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory.
items.body:
Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 389-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
The D-backs (81-74) gained a game on Philadelphia (85-70) for the third spot in the National League wild-card race but are still four games back with seven games to play.
Yankees starter and American League Cy Young candidate Cam Schlittler gave up three hits and three runs (one earned) in six innings, leaving when his pitch count reached 98. His season high is 106.
Schlittler struck out three and walked six while lowering his ERA to an American League-leading 1.94. He has given up one earned run or fewer in each of his last eight starts.
Arizona starter Brandon Pfaadt gave up four singles and one run in 4 1/3 innings, leaving after the Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth. Ben Rice hit a sacrifice fly off Justin Martinez to break a scoreless tie. Pfaadt struck out three and walked one.
The D-backs broke up Schlittler's no-hitter with a two-run fifth. Both runs scored after Schlittler's one-out fielding error.
Arenado had Arizona's first hit, a line single to left field with one out, before Tim Tawa pushed a bunt toward the mound. Schlittler could not field the ball cleanly and both runners were safe.
Lawlar lined a two-out triple to left-center on a 99 mph fastball for a 2-1 lead.
Ramos and Wells homered in the sixth to put the Yankees in front 3-2.
The D-backs tied it in the sixth when Ketel Marte and Gabriel Moreno drew four-pitch walks and Geraldo Perdomo beat out a two-strike bunt single to load the bases. Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly before Schlittler struck out Arenado and Tawa with runners on second and third.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Macron, Carney to meet in French Atlantic archipelago in signal to Trump
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: President Emmanuel Macron visits the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Sunday, where he is due to meet Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image on social media showing the archipelago covered by the American flag.
items.body:
President Emmanuel Macron visits the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Sunday, where he is due to meet Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump posted an image on social media showing the archipelago covered by the American flag.
Macron's visit, the first by a French president since Francois Hollande travelled there in 2014, comes as Canada seeks to deepen ties with the European Union amid trade tensions with the United States and a deterioration in relations with Washington under Trump.
Located off Canada's Atlantic coast, Saint Pierre and Miquelon is France's only remaining territory in North America. French officials said the trip would underscore France's sovereignty over the archipelago and highlight its close relationship with Canada.
"For a territory of 5,800 inhabitants, it is rare to find so many issues that are important for France as a whole concentrated in a place of this size: France's geostrategic presence in the North Atlantic, at the doorstep of the United States and the Arctic, maritime sovereignty, adaptation to climate change; and cooperation with Canada," a French presidency official told reporters.
Diplomats said the visit, which Macron was undertaking on his way to the annual United Nations General Assembly gathering of world leaders, would also carry symbolic weight after Trump posted a map depicting the United States, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean draped in the U.S. flag and labelled "United States of America".
The image included Saint Pierre and Miquelon and several French Caribbean territories.
France chose not to publicly respond to the post at the time.
Macron and Carney are expected to discuss the energy crisis and Canada's increasingly close relationship with the European Union after the bloc opened the door to Ottawa becoming its first associate member.
Any move towards deeper integration is likely to face hurdles. More than a decade after the EU and Canada agreed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and nine years after its provisional application began, several EU member states have yet to ratify the accord, including France.

items.title: Russian election, cast as test of support for Ukraine war, enters final day
items.author: Andrew Osborn
items.creator: Andrew Osborn
items.summary: The State Duma vote, the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, is likely to be presented by the Kremlin as evidence of public backing for Putin's policies and for the war.
items.body:
A [USN:L6N451112 TEXT:"parliamentary election"] that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for Russia's war in Ukraine entered its third and final day on Sunday, with the ruling United Russia party expected to retain its dominance in a political system critics say does not tolerate dissent.
The State Duma vote, the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, i[USN:L6N45A0MN TEXT:"s likely to be presented by the Kremlin"] as evidence of public backing for Putin's policies and for the war, Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two, now in its fifth year with no sign of ending soon.
Most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot. Those who did run from the liberal Yabloko party, which has polled in the single digits in recent years but hoped to tap into war fatigue, said they [USN:L6N4530O5 TEXT:"feared for their freedom"] after courts handed long jail terms to two senior party figures before the vote for comments about the conflict deemed illegal by authorities.
Discrediting the army or spreading what authorities regard as fake news are punishable by lengthy prison sentences.
The Kremlin says national unity and some censorship are necessary during what it calls its special military operation in Ukraine. It casts the conflict as part of an existential struggle with a hostile West and says Ukrainian intelligence services and other enemies are stepping up efforts to stir unrest inside Russia.
PERMITTED OPPOSITION PARTIES COULD BENEFIT Putin on Friday [USN:L1N45A0ZW TEXT:"accused Ukraine"] of trying to interfere in the election, citing what he said was a Ukrainian strike on the home of an election official in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region that killed Elena Astanina, the official. Reuters could not independently verify details of the attack and there was no immediate comment from Kyiv.
Russian electoral officials also said on Saturday that an online voting system in Moscow [USN:L1N45B029 TEXT:"had come under cyberattack."] Kyiv, which has suspended elections under martial law, has dismissed the Russian vote as a "pseudo election".
Despite what most experts see as the election's predictable outcome, the NEST think-tank in Berlin, co-founded by Kremlin critic Mikhail Khodorkovsky, whom Russian authorities have designated "a foreign agent", said the vote could still produce awkward moments for the Kremlin at a time of [USN:L8N456064 TEXT:"economic strain"].
"The consequences of the war are increasingly being felt within the country, and [USN:L6N44V10B TEXT:"accumulated anxiety and frustration"] may translate into votes for the systemic opposition parties that the Kremlin has allowed to remain on the ballot," it said in a note.
It said the Communist party and the New People party could attract votes the authorities would prefer to go to United Russia. Both parties have consistently voted in line with United Russia on major issues.
Putin told the nation i[USN:S8N44V093 TEXT:"n a televised address"] before the election that the vote would underline support for Russian troops fighting in Ukraine.
"Your choice, and your will, will once again demonstrate that millions of people stand behind our soldiers, that we are a united people bound together by shared values, historical memory, and love for our homeland, and that no one will succeed in dividing or intimidating us," said Putin.
Initial results are expected to start emerging at around 1800 GMT on Sunday, with more complete results available on Monday.

items.title: China's CXMT says new memory-chip platform enters mass production
items.author: Che Pan, Eduardo Baptista
items.creator: Che Pan, Eduardo Baptista
items.summary: Chinese DRAM chipmaker CXMT said on Sunday its fifth-generation technology platform had entered mass production, a claimed breakthrough that could help China build a stronger competitor to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology in the global market for memory chips.
items.body:
Chinese DRAM chipmaker CXMT (688825.SS) said on Sunday its fifth-generation technology platform had entered mass production, a claimed breakthrough that could help China build a stronger competitor to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology in the global market for memory chips.
DRAM, or dynamic random-access memory, is the short-term working memory that phones, computers and other devices use to run apps and programs.
The new platform is designed to make more powerful memory chips at lower cost and with less power use. CXMT, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market this year, said it would give electronics makers an additional source of supply for chips used in smartphones and other devices.
CXMT, China's leading producer of DRAM, said the new platform packs the tiny structures that store data closer together, allowing more memory to fit on each chip and more individual chips to be made from each silicon wafer.
The Hefei-based memory-chip maker said it had reduced the spacing of key features in the part of the chip that stores data to 11.95 nanometres, or about 12 billionths of a metre.
It achieved this using "quadruple patterning," a process that repeats several manufacturing steps to produce finer circuit patterns.
"Our process capability is now on par with the most advanced mass-produced nodes out there in the industry," Luo Xiaodong, CXMT's vice president and head of its marketing centre, said at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei.
CXMT UNVEILS TWO NEW CHIPS CXMT also unveiled two 24-gigabit LPDDR5X products made on the new platform. LPDDR5X is a power-saving type of DRAM used mainly in smartphones and other portable electronics.
The products each hold 50% more data than CXMT's previous equivalent products and are already in mass production, the company said. They are offered in two package formats for different smartphone and portable-device designs.
CXMT said the platform can produce at least 50% more gross chip dies per wafer than its fourth-generation platform, using an 8-gigabit-chip baseline.
That measures the potential number of chips made from a wafer before defective units are excluded, rather than the proportion that pass final testing.
CXMT said it developed the platform using computer simulations and joint work with Chinese chip-equipment makers on critical production steps.
The advance comes as Beijing seeks to reduce reliance on foreign semiconductor technology and US export controls since 2022 have restricted China's access to certain advanced chipmaking equipment and related software.

items.title: Nationals tally four in 11th; outlast struggling Cardinals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and the Washington Nationals beat the Cardinals 8-5 on Saturday night in St. Louis.
items.body:
Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and the Washington Nationals beat the Cardinals 8-5 on Saturday night in St. Louis.
Keibert Ruiz singled leading off the 11th against Gordon Graceffo (8-2), moving designated runner Yohandy Morales to third. Nasim Nunez walked to load the bases and Jacob Young reached on a catcher's interference call against Leo Bernal, plating the go-ahead run.
Daylen Lile struck out, but Tena smacked a double to left center and the lead expanded to 7-4. CJ Abrams was walked intentionally and Dylan Crews hit a sacrifice fly to right that would have been more damaging if not for a diving catch by Jordan Walker.
JJ Wetherholt singled home a run leading off the bottom half against Riley Cornelio. Alec Burleson singled and Jose Fermin walked to load the bases.
But Ivan Herrera and Jordan Walker struck out, and Will Dion came on, getting Bernal to fly out for his first major league save.
Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Lile homered for Washington (73-82), which has won six of seven.
Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.
At the top of the order, Fermin and Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis (75-80), which has lost four straight.
Vivas singled home a run in the top of the tenth and Masyn Winn matched him in the bottom half.
St. Louis tied it in the ninth. Nathan Church led off with a double to left and scored on Pedro Pages' single.
Trailing 3-0, the Cardinals rallied in the seventh. Winn reached on a throwing error by third baseman Vivas and went to second on a ground out. Pages hit a dribbler toward third and pitcher Richard Lovelady threw wildly to first. Winn scored and Pages went to second. One out later Fermin singled, scoring Pages to make it 3-2.
James Wood opened the game with a single and Lile followed with a two-run homer.
The Nationals added a run in the sixth. Vivas singled with one out and Andres Chaparro followed with an infield hit. After Ruiz grounded into a fielder's choice, Nunez singled, scoring Vivas to make it 3-0.
Washington's Andrew Alvarez tossed six shutout innings. He gave up five hits and tied his season high with eight strikeouts.
Cardinals starter Michael McGreevy gave up two runs on five hits over four innings.
--Field Level Media

items.title: IOC chief Coventry gives thumbs-up to Asian Games accommodation despite criticism
items.author: Ian Ransom
items.creator: Ian Ransom
items.summary: International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry threw her weight behind the beleaguered Asian Games organisers on Sunday, saying she was impressed with the athletes' accommodation in Nagoya despite criticism from some competitors.
items.body:
International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry threw her weight behind the beleaguered Asian Games organisers on Sunday, saying she was impressed with the athletes' accommodation in Nagoya despite criticism from some competitors.
Japanese organisers scrapped initial plans for a [USN:L6N4590KW TEXT:"dedicated Athletes' Village"] in an effort to control costs, opting instead to house 17,000 athletes and officials across hotels, shipping-container-style huts and a cruise ship.
Several athletes have complained about cramped living quarters and undersized beds, but Coventry gave the facilities a resounding thumbs-up after inspecting the accommodation at Garden Pier.
"The cabins are quiet, they're very cool. The air conditioning is working well. The flooring and the walls are beautiful," Coventry told reporters afterwards.
"It's better than some of the (athletes') villages I've ever stayed in. So I think to be very fair to Japan and to the organising committee, I was really impressed.
"I'd only been reading everything that had been said, and I was expecting something completely different to when I walked in. And I hope that you guys will get to experience the same thing."
Coventry, a former Olympic swimming champion, said this was not the first time athletes had been housed in such modular setups even though these were slightly smaller than the cabins used in Milano Cortina Winter Olympics earlier this year.
"We had cabins in 2000, my very first (Olympic) Games in Australia. It's not a new concept. I'm not necessarily concerned about the look."
The overarching priority remained ensuring that competitors enjoyed a positive overall experience, the Zimbabwean added.
"I think what athletes expect from us is that there needs to be a minimum level of standards, right? And we're going to try and work with everybody to do that."

items.title: Trump seeks to bring health-research funding under his control, Politico reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is seeking to bring a major part of national funding for health research under the control of his political appointees, Politico reported on Saturday.
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump is seeking to bring a major part of national funding for health research under the control of his political appointees, Politico reported on Saturday.
Trump has directed his budget director, Russ Vought, to draft an executive order to create a board that would decide which grants would be funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the news outlet said, citing two administration officials familiar with the meeting.
The board would include NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya and Vought, the director of the White House Office of Management and Budget, and would be required to reach unanimous decisions on grant awards, the report said.
The proposed arrangement would give Vought a direct role in determining how the health research agency distributes its congressionally-appropriated money, the report added.
The Office of Management and Budget, the White House and the Health and Human Services Department that oversees the NIH did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
The reported move comes amid mounting criticism of the US government's research [USN:L1N3Y60VZ TEXT:"funding cuts"], undertaken last year to target federal spending at major universities, resulting in the freezing or cancellation of grants at numerous institutions.
The Trump administration says these cuts are necessary to ensure the government funds only solid science and to reverse years of misguided priorities.

items.title: Rockies score 4 times in seventh to rally past Mariners
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as the Colorado Rockies edged the Seattle Mariners 5-3 on Saturday night in Denver.
items.body:
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as the Colorado Rockies edged the Seattle Mariners 5-3 on Saturday night in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado (57-98).
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle (72-83), which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Before the game, the Rockies honored Hall of Fame first baseman Todd Helton with the unveiling of a statue of him in front of Coors Field. The statue depicts Helton celebrating after catching the last out of the 2007 NLCS that sent Colorado to the World Series.
Colorado lefty Jose Quintana made first start since May 24, missing nearly four months with a left elbow sprain. He allowed three runs on five hits in four innings and gave up two home runs.
Raleigh gave the Mariners a 2-0 lead in the first with a two-run homer, his 23rd of the season, and Arozarena made it 3-0 in the third inning with his 26th long ball.
But Colorado capitalized on bad Seattle defense to get a run back in the bottom of the inning.
With one out, Jake McCarthy laid down a bunt single that Raleigh fielded and threw wildly to first, allowing McCarthy to advance to third. Connor Norby hit a fly ball to short right, and McCarthy raced home when Dominic Canzone's throw short-hopped Raleigh.
That was all Seattle starter Bryce Miller gave up. He allowed an unearned run on four hits and struck out six in 5 1/3 innings.
The Rockies rallied in the seventh to take the lead against reliever Jose Ferrer (4-4). Zac Veen and Adael Amador hit one-out singles and Veen came around on McCarthy's groundout.
With two outs, Norby delivered an infield single, bringing up TJ Rumfield, who drove in Amador with a single up the middle to knot the game at 3-3.
Hunter Goodman walked to load the bases and Carrigg hit a two-run single to center off Cooper Criswell to put Colorado in front.
Norby and Rumfield each had a pair of singles for Colorado, who did not record an extra-base hit in the game.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Townsend hit by pitch roller while warming up in Thai league
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up with his Prachuap teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on Saturday.
items.body:
Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up with his Prachuap teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on Saturday.
The 35-year-old avoided serious injury and later made a brief appearance in the match at Pattani.
The former Tottenham Hotspur player did not see the roller, driven by a ground staff member, coming towards him when he stepped out of the practice area to attempt a pass.
The roller knocked Townsend over and drove up his legs nearly to his waist before the driver jumped off and tried to lift it off the player.
Townsend got back up and continued practicing, and came on as a late substitute while Prachuap cruised to a 3-0 victory.
"Turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all," Townsend later wrote on Instagram, joking about the English side Stoke City's reputation as a tough place for visiting teams to play.

その他、ボローニャとトリノは１─１で引き分けた。

items.title: Paramount settlement talks include plan to keep company in California
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The settlement talks between Paramount Skydance Corp. and California officials over the lawsuit challenging the Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. acquisition have included a promise by the company to stay ...
items.body: By Josh Sisco The settlement talks between Paramount Skydance Corp. and California officials over the lawsuit challenging the Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. acquisition have included a promise by the company to stay in the state. Other terms being considered include an editorial board to monitor CNN, Paramount releasing 30 movies a year in theaters, an agreement to not negotiate distribution for all of the company’s channels together and a sale of some cable channels, according to a person familiar with the discussions, who asked not to be identified because the talks aren’t public. Paramount Chief Executive Officer David Ellison and California Attorney General Rob Bonta have personally been involved in the settlement discussions, according to two people familiar with the matter. Some of the settlement talks have not included other states or the Writers Guild, which are also suing to block the Warner Bros. acquisition, the people said. Some of the parties do not approve all of the terms being discussed.  Paramount is headquartered in New York, but has substantial operations in Los Angeles. Ellison and his chief legal officer, Makan Delrahim, have done little to quell rampant stories in the media that the company is considering relocating to another state. Any settlement would likely need the support of all 12 Democratic states challenging the merger, along with the Writers Guild, said the people, who were granted anonymity to discuss a confidential process. Paramount shares rose as much as 8.7% in after-hours trading on Friday following a Wall Street Journal report that the company was in advanced talks with California officials about settling the litigation. Reuters reported that a settlement could come this weekend or Monday.  A California judge also ordered settlement talks, which are formally scheduled for Oct. 14-15. A trial date isn’t scheduled until March. A spokesperson for Paramount declined to comment. A spokesperson for Bonta said Friday his office “cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their alleged substance.” Paramount has previously made public offers to release 30 films a year in theaters and to increase production of TV shows. Bonta has repeatedly said he doesn’t favor those types of behavioral remedies because they are hard to enforce. The attorney general has said he prefers structural changes, such as a sale of assets. Some opponents of the merger have called on Bonta to not settle. US Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts said in a social media post that it “would be a massive mistake to cave on the Paramount merger.” In his own post, actor Mark Ruffalo urged Bonta to not let “this lousy deal filled with empty promises go forward.”  The attorney general told Bloomberg TV on Thursday that a sale of some intellectual property “could be a component” of a settlement. The deal would bring well-known Warner Bros. movie franchises such as DC Comics, Harry Potter and The Lord of the Rings into the Paramount fold. Bloomberg News reported last month that Paramount has weighed selling cable channels such as HGTV and the Food Network as a way to settle the litigation. Investment bankers have approached would-be buyers about Warner’s New Line Cinema division. Bidders have also been interested in the Comedy Central cable network. Paramount will be required to pay late fees of $7 million a day to Warner Bros. starting at the end of this month if a deal is not reached. A failed acquisition would force it to pay $7 billion to Warner Bros. “Paramount has strong reasons to reach a workable compromise,” Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Geetha Ranganathan wrote in a research note Friday.

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ヤンキース、ジャッジ外野手が10日間のＩＬ入り
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ヤンキースは１９日、アーロン・ジャッジ外野手（３４）を右ふくらはぎの肉離れで１０日間の負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）に登録した。１７日にさかのぼって適用される。

ア・リーグ最優秀選手（ＭＶＰ）に３度選出されている主将のジャッジは、１６日のツインズ戦で右脚下部の張りを訴え、六回に交代。試合後には一回から違和感があり、プレーを続けようとしたものの、その後アーロン・ブーン監督に状況を伝えたと明かしていた。

ジャッジは今季、肋骨の負傷で３カ月以上離脱。今月８日に復帰したばかりだった。復帰後は７試合で２３打数４安打（打率１割７分４厘）、１本塁打、３打点の成績にとどまっていた。

同選手は「けがから復帰後、調子を上げようとしているときはうまくいかないこともある」とコメント。「今回のことが小さな問題であり、近いうちに復帰できることを願っている」と述べた。順調に回復すれば、最短で９月２７日のレギュラーシーズン最終戦で戦列復帰が可能。今季は６６試合に出場し、打率２割４分１厘、１８本塁打、４１打点の成績を残している。

ヤンキースはこの日、マイナー傘下３Ａスクラントンからマックス・シューマン外野手（２９）を昇格させた。

items.title: Companies avoid selling long-term bonds investors are clamoring for
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Declining sales volume of bonds maturing in 30 years or more could result in some companies having to refinance their debt more often as their liabilities become shorter-term. And it’s left a void of ...
items.body: By Emily Graffeo, Caleb Mutua, Finbarr Flynn and Ronan Martin Investors are clamoring for the kind of debt companies are reluctant to sell now: longer-term bonds.  When insurance broker Aon Inc. sold $2 billion of 30-year notes on Monday, investors placed orders for $10 billion of securities. And when drugmaker GSK Plc sold $500 million of 30-year debt earlier this month, demand was about ten times larger than supply.   That demand is higher than most of the market has seen this year. On average, orders for high-grade US corporate bonds have equaled about four times the notes for sale in 2026.   It’s all being driven by surging yields globally, especially on longer-term bonds, after inflation fears have risen. Central banks, including the Federal Reserve this week, are boosting rates to try to tamp down longer-term borrowing costs. But in the meantime, companies are reluctant to sell bonds that will force them to make relatively heavy interest payments for decades. By the same token, investors are eager to buy bonds that will generate high income for years.  “The opportunity is there now to extend out the curve, and we have been buyers of long investment grade corporate bonds,” said Matt Eagan, portfolio manager at Loomis, Sayles & Co. “The challenge is the scarcity of this kind of paper,” with the exception of artificial-intelligence related issuance.  Just 5% of the US investment-grade bonds sold in the first half of September mature in at least 30 years, or about $108.3 billion of debt, the smallest share for the period since at least 2020, according to Bloomberg News analysis. A similar trend is playing out in Europe and Asia.   The 30-year Treasury yield has risen nearly 0.5 percentage point this year, closing at a post-financial crisis high of about 5.37% a day before the Fed hiked interest rates by a quarter percentage point, its first increase in three years.   The US central bank on Wednesday signaled another increase is coming this year as higher oil prices and the prolonged Iran war fuel inflation concerns. On Sept. 10, the European Central Bank lifted interest rates for the second time since the conflict began, with traders now fully pricing three more hikes by October 2027. It’s not just the Fed that’s to blame for higher borrowing costs. Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. have flooded the market with long-dated debt this year, crowding out even sovereign issuers while investors unload existing holdings to buy higher-yielding debt from immensely profitable hyperscalers. Years of falling interest rates reshaped the US investment-grade market as companies sold ever-longer-term debt to lock in cheap borrowing costs for decades, boosting average maturities in the US high-grade market to a peak of 12.4 years, according to a report from Barclays strategists on Friday.  That shift is now gradually reversing as borrowing costs rise, with the average maturity in the market shrinking to 10.3 years. Duration, a measure of a bond price’s sensitivity to changes in rates that is connected with factors including maturities, has similarly shrunk in recent years, to about 6.5 now from around 8.8 five years ago.  “There is a cost to doing longer dated tenors and with yields having moved higher, companies are looking to minimize this cost,” said Fabianna Del Canto, co-head of capital markets for EMEA at Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. Declining sales volume of bonds maturing in 30 years or more could result in some companies having to refinance their debt more often as their liabilities become shorter-term. And it’s left a void of supply for life insurers that seek long-dated debt to match the maturities of annuities, and pension plans funding future payouts to retirees. “It creates a bit of a challenge for insurance and pension investors,” said Dan Mead, head of investment grade syndicate at Bank of America. The tension is playing out in private debt markets as well, where investors that tend to be insurance companies are hungry for duration. The average tenor of new private placement bond issues in 2026 has shrunk to around 8.9 years, down from 13.2 years in 2021.  European borrowers are also shortening tenors. About 80% of debt sold this year comes due within a decade, up from 65% last year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.   And companies in Asia Pacific are selling less longer-dated dollar debt. Data compiled by Bloomberg shows there’s been just one one dollar bond sold in the first half of September by an APAC company that matures in 10 years or longer and can’t be called: a $500 million note from Norinchukin Bank.  That’s the lowest total for longer-dated note sales for the period in 15 years by companies in the region in dollars, and compares with about $6.7 billion in 2025 by this time in the month, the data show. Back in the US, investors await Sysco Corp.’s $17 billion issue as soon as next week, including increasingly rare 30- and 40-year fixed rate notes, to fund its $29 billion acquisition of wholesaler Jetro Restaurant Depot LLC. Citigroup’s bond sale this week saw a peak of about $18 billion of demand for its longest maturity, $4.5 billion of 11-year notes.  By and large, issuers are bypassing long-dated debt in favor of maturities of five or seven years, or even shorter, in hopes that borrowing costs will fall down the road. “There have been and continue to be a number of borrowers where even for bigger deals, they are trying to limit the long end component” said Teddy Hodgson, global co-head of investment grade debt capital markets at Morgan Stanley.

items.title: サッカー＝フライブルク鈴木が同点ゴール、ボルシアＭＧ町野も得点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは１９日、各地で試合を行い、フライブルクは先発した鈴木唯人のゴールで堂安律と小杉啓太の所属するアイントラハト・フランクフルトと２─２の引き分けに持ち込んだ。

試合は前半１０分、先発した堂安のアシストからユネス・エブヌタリブが決めて、フランクフルトが先制。その後、互いに１ゴールずつ奪った後半３分、左クロスにファーで走り込んだ鈴木が、ボレーで得点ランキングトップタイの今季４点目を決めた。

鈴木は後半３９分までプレー。同僚の後藤啓介は同じ時間からピッチに入った。山本理仁はベンチ入りしなかった。小杉はフル出場し、堂安は後半１６分までプレーした。

ボルシアＭＧはマインツに３─４で敗れ、開幕から４連敗。先発した板倉滉との交代で後半３９分から入った町野修斗がアディショナルタイムにＰＫを決めたが、それ以上の反撃には至らなかった。チームメートの橋岡大樹は後半３１分からプレーし、宇野禅斗はベンチ入りしなかった。

マインツの佐野海舟はフル出場し、チームの３点目をアシストした。同僚の川崎颯太はベンチを外れた。

その他、ドルトムントはシュツットガルトに１─０で勝利し、開幕４戦全勝。ブレーメンはアウクスブルクを３─２で下し、ハンブルガーＳＶはケルンに２─１で競り勝った。

items.title: Japan win first gold of home Asian Games in men's individual triathlon
items.author: Amlan Chakraborty
items.creator: Amlan Chakraborty
items.summary: Hosts Japan won the first gold of the Aichi-Nagoa Asian Games after Takumi Hojo powered to victory in the men's individual triathlon on Sunday.
items.body:
Hosts Japan won the first gold of the Aichi-Nagoa Asian Games after Takumi Hojo powered to victory in the men's individual triathlon on Sunday.
Hojo exited the warm waters of Mikawa Bay in fourth position and the bike section in fifth before breaking clear on the run to win by nine seconds ahead of China's Zhang Xirui, who took silver. Kazakhstan’s Arlan Zhanabay finished a further six seconds behind for the bronze.
“I was really fired up – even the rain held off, and I was in top form right up until I stood on the starting line,” said Hojo, who won the mixed relay gold at the Hangzhou Games three years ago.
“I’d planned to attack using my strengths right until the end."
“As it’s our first gold medal, it’s given the Japanese team a real boost, and we’ve managed to pass the baton on to the women and our teammates for the relay.”
Uzbek Aleksandr Kurishov was first out of the water but faded on the bike and eventually finished 20th.
Swimming competitions also got underway at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre on Sunday.

items.title: Rangers stay hot, take down Blue Jays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Texas Rangers won for the sixth time in their past seven games, defeating the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2 on Saturday in Arlington, Texas.
items.body:
The Texas Rangers won for the sixth time in their past seven games, defeating the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2 on Saturday in Arlington, Texas.
Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings.
Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five innings for the Blue Jays (76-79), who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Josh Jung gave Texas (78-77) a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.
The Rangers added two more runs despite not recording a hit in the second frame. Wyatt Langford drew a walk to lead off and, one out later, Nicky Lopez caught a pitch off his right foot. Langford came around to score on a fielder's choice when shortstop Andres Gimenez missed the throw to second base on Danny Jansen's grounder.
Lopez, who advanced to third on Gimenez's error, scored on Soriano's wild pitch to make it 3-0.
Toronto didn't get its first baserunner until the fourth inning on a walk to Vladimir Guerrero Jr., and it took until the sixth for its first hit, against Nathan Eovaldi.
A curveball from Eovaldi caught Gimenez on the foot to lead off the sixth frame. Gimenez moved to second on Brett Bateman's one-out single, and Alejandro Kirk brought him in with a two-out base hit to center to cut it to 3-1.
The hosts widened the gap in the bottom half. Jung was hit by a pitch, Brandon Nimmo singled and Langford's double off the left field wall scored Jung to push the advantage to 4-1.
That ended Soriano's night, replaced by Paul Sewald. After striking out Jake Burger for the first out, Sewald intentionally walked Lopez to load the bases. He then hit Danny Jansen, forcing in Nimmo. Evan Carter then connected for a sacrifice fly that brought Langford home to extend it to 6-1.
Toronto's Davis Schneider pinch-hit a solo shot to left center to narrow it to 6-2 in the seventh.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ronald Acuna Jr.’s late grand slam leads Braves past Astros
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start, and the visiting Atlanta Braves lowered their magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating the Houston Astros 6-3 on Saturday.
items.body:
Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start, and the visiting Atlanta Braves lowered their magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating the Houston Astros 6-3 on Saturday.
The Braves (91-64) secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the National League East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday.
The Astros (77-78) fell below .500 for the first time since Aug. 26 and dropped a game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West after Texas beat the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2.
Isaac Paredes, who recorded both RBIs for the Astros in their 6-2 loss on Friday, homered with two outs in the bottom of the first inning off Holmes (10-5). The clout was his 22nd home run of the season and gave Houston a 1-0 lead.
Two innings later, Paredes struck again. He flipped an RBI single to right with one out in the third, scoring Jeremy Pena. Pena had opened the frame with a triple to left-center.
Holmes stranded runners in the first and second innings but settled down after Paredes doubled the Astros' lead to 2-0. Holmes retired the final two batters of the third and faced the minimum in the fourth and sixth despite allowing base hits in each frame. Holmes induced Yainer Diaz to ground into a double play, erasing a leadoff single by Jose Altuve in the bottom of the sixth.
Holmes allowed two runs on eight hits and struck out four over six innings.
Astros right-hander Hayden Wesneski appeared set to make the lead stand. He stranded runners on the corners in the top of the first and retired seven consecutive batters entering the sixth.
But Drake Baldwin opened the sixth with a single. He scored two batters later when Matt Olson chased Wesneski with an RBI single.
Acuna struck the decisive blow an inning later when he launched a fastball from Astros reliever Bryan Abreu 411 feet to left-center to give the Braves a 5-2 lead. Three of those runs were charged to Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3), who loaded the bases before Abreu entered with one out, struck out Baldwin, but allowed the two-out grand slam to Acuna.
Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for the Braves.
Wesneski allowed one run on four hits with four strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings.
Altuve went 3-for-4 for Houston.
--Field Level Media

北アフリカのスペイン飛地領セウタで18日早朝、警察がビーチで寝泊まりしていた数百人の移民を港に設けられた仮設施設へ移送する作業を始めた。限られた収容枠を巡って移民らが押し合う中、緊迫した場面が展開された。

作業は現地時間午前7時前に開始され、機動隊とスペイン軍が投入された。

映像では、指定されたルートに入ろうとする人々でごった返し、押し合いになる様子が捉えられている。警察は威嚇のため空に向けて暴徒鎮圧用の弾を発射し、複数の移民を警棒で殴打。その後、事態が沈静化し、作業が再開された。

仮設シェルターの枠を求めてビーチで夜を明かした移民らは、移送が始まると当初は拍手で迎えたが、限られた収容枠を巡って争いが起き、もみ合いに発展した。

当局はセウタの港に1700人を収容できる新たな仮設住宅を建設した。NGOによると、依然として数千人が住まいを持たず、野宿を続けている。

移民の大半は成人男性と少年で占められる。仮設住宅は成人男性向けに設計されているため、未成年者は分離され、別の場所に収容されている。

あるNGOの推計では、約4000人の移民がなお浜辺や歩道といった屋外にとどまっており、今回設置された仮設住宅だけでは足りないという。NGO関係者らは、当局は大半の移民がモロッコへ自発的に帰還すると見込んでいるのではないかと述べた。

items.title: ノースカロライナ大学基金、運用益37.8%－15年前のスペースX投資寄与
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米ノースカロライナ大学（UNC）の基金は、6月終了の会計年度に37.8%の運用収益率を上げた。15年以上前に宇宙開発会社スペースXに投資していたことが寄与し、他の大学基金を上回る運用成績となった。

公表資料によると、世界株式のリターンに支えられ、「並外れた1年」となったほか、「スペースXへの投資が極めて強い追い風となった」という。

運用収益率は、ウィルシャー・トラスト・ユニバース・コンパリソン・サービスが推計する5億ドル（約780億円）超の大学基金の中央値18.9%（手数料控除前）の2倍となった。

大学側はコメントを控えた。事情に詳しい関係者が以前明らかにしたところによると、基金はスペースXによる過去最大規模の新規株式公開（IPO）前に同社株約10億ドル相当を売却。スペースXに投資するファンドへの数百万ドルの出資が、巨額のリターンにつながった。

ブルームバーグが8月に報じたところによると、UNCの基金はなお10億ドル超の同社株を保有している。スペースX株は18日に152.71ドルで取引を終えた。IPO価格の135ドルから13.1%上昇し、時価総額は2兆ドルを超えた。

6月30日までの会計年度の運用成績を各基金が公表するのに伴い、スペースXのほか、AI業界をけん引するOpenAI、アンソロピックへの投資比率次第では、他の大学基金でもリターンが急増したことが明らかになる可能性が高まっている。

原題：UNC Endowment Fund Jumps 37.8%, Driven by Early SpaceX Stake（抜粋）

items.body:
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 6-5 victory over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Saturday.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates (78-77).
Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals (67-88). Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Flores led off the eighth by singling on a 0-2 pitch before Lowe homered off Royals reliever Steven Cruz (2-4) for his fourth blast in five games and 33rd of the season to give the Pirates a 6-5 lead.
The Pirates had taken a 2-0 lead in the second inning when Simon hit his first career home run in 42 games, a two-run shot just inside the left field foul pole.
In the third, Jensen set a Royals rookie record with his 25th home run of the season, trimming Pittsburgh's advantage to 2-1.
Mangum's two-run homer in the fourth to left extended Pittsburgh's lead to 4-1.
The Royals trimmed their deficit to 4-3 in the fifth. Witt legged out a slow roller to third, and after Caglianone walked, Pittsburgh starter Bubba Chandler was relieved by Brandon Eisert. Witt and Caglianone executed a double steal to put runners on second and third.
Pasquantino's groundout plated Witt, and one batter later, Michael Massey's sacrifice bunt brought home Caglianone. Ryan O'Hearn made a slick glove flip through his legs to Eisert, who tagged first base just before a head-first sliding Massey.
In the seventh, Kansas City collected four hits and scored two runs to take a 5-4 lead on RBI singles by Caglianone and Loftin.
Royals starter Noah Cameron allowed four runs on seven hits with two walks and six strikeouts. Chandler yielded three runs on eight hits with a walk and six strikeouts.
